units.text: INT. HUSBAND - CONTINUOUS
Basildon is quite as bad; he is as domestic as if he was a bachelor.
units.name: LADY BASILDON

units.text: Pressing LADY BASILDON’S hand .
My poor Olivia! We have married perfect husbands, and we are well punished for it.
units.name: MRS. MARCHMONT

units.text: I should have thought it was the husbands who were punished.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Drawing herself up .
Oh, dear no! They are as happy as possible! And as for trusting us, it is tragic how much they trust us.
units.name: MRS. MARCHMONT

units.text: Perfectly tragic!
units.name: LADY BASILDON

units.text: Or comic, Lady Basildon?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Certainly not comic, Lord Goring. How unkind of you to suggest such a thing!
units.name: LADY BASILDON

units.text: I am afraid Lord Goring is in the camp of the enemy, as usual. I saw him talking to that Mrs. Cheveley when he came in.
units.name: MRS. MARCHMONT

units.text: Handsome woman, Mrs. Cheveley!
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Stiffly .
Please don’t praise other women in our presence. You might wait for us to do that!
units.name: LADY BASILDON

units.text: I did wait.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Well, we are not going to praise her. I hear she went to the Opera on Monday night, and told Tommy Rufford at supper that, as far as she could see, London Society was entirely made up of dowdies and dandies.
units.name: MRS. MARCHMONT

units.text: She is quite right, too. The men are all dowdies and the women are all dandies, aren’t they?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: After a pause .
Oh! do you really think that is what Mrs. Cheveley meant?
units.name: MRS. MARCHMONT

units.text: Of course. And a very sensible remark for Mrs. Cheveley to make, too.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Enter MABEL CHILTERN.
She joins the group .

Why are you talking about Mrs. Cheveley? Everybody is talking about Mrs. Cheveley! Lord Goring says—what did you say, Lord Goring, about Mrs. Cheveley? Oh! I remember, that she was a genius in the daytime and a beauty at night.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: What a horrid combination! So very unnatural!
units.name: LADY BASILDON

units.text: In her most dreamy manner .
I like looking at geniuses, and listening to beautiful people.
units.name: MRS. MARCHMONT

units.text: Ah! that is morbid of you, Mrs. Marchmont!
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Brightening to a look of real pleasure .
I am so glad to hear you say that. Marchmont and I have been married for seven years, and he has never once told me that I was morbid. Men are so painfully unobservant!
units.name: MRS. MARCHMONT

units.text: Turning to her .
I have always said, dear Margaret, that you were the most morbid person in London.
units.name: LADY BASILDON

units.text: Ah! but you are always sympathetic, Olivia!
units.name: MRS. MARCHMONT

units.text: Is it morbid to have a desire for food? I have a great desire for food. Lord Goring, will you give me some supper?
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: With pleasure, Miss Mabel.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Moves away with her .
How horrid you have been! You have never talked to me the whole evening!
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: How could I? You went away with the child-diplomatist.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: You might have followed us. Pursuit would have been only polite. I don’t think I like you at all this evening!
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: I like you immensely.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Well, I wish you’d show it in a more marked way!
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: They go downstairs .
Olivia, I have a curious feeling of absolute faintness. I think I should like some supper very much. I know I should like some supper.
units.name: MRS. MARCHMONT

units.text: I am positively dying for supper, Margaret!
units.name: LADY BASILDON

units.text: Men are so horribly selfish, they never think of these things.
units.name: MRS. MARCHMONT

units.text: Men are grossly material, grossly material!
units.name: LADY BASILDON

units.text: The VICOMTE DE NANJAC enters from the music-room with some other guests .
After having carefully examined all the people present , he approaches LADY BASILDON.
May I have the honour of taking you down to supper, Comtesse?
units.name: VICOMTE DE NANJAC
